neighbours.label: bare ' it' or ' that' right after has/have/there's, pointing at an unnamed quality or situation ('has it', 'has that rare...', 'there's that')
fire: Few bars in this city have it, but this corner pub really has it.
Her latest album has that warm, dusty feel of old vinyl.
He lost his job and his car, so there's that.
Not every singer has it, but this young woman clearly does.
Rumor has it that the mayor will resign next week.
This old hotel has that quiet charm you rarely find anymore.
The kid has it, the coach said after the first practice.
My brother is broke and unemployed, and then there's that.
quiet: Few bars in this city have live jazz, but this corner pub does.
Her latest album has a warm, dusty feel like old vinyl.
He lost his job and his car, and he moved back home.
Not every singer reads music, but this young woman clearly does.
The mayor said that it would rain during the parade next week.
This old hotel offers quiet rooms you rarely find anymore.
The coach watched it twice after the first practice.
My brother bought that guitar, and then sold it to me.

notes: Probe: 'definitely has it' 1.03, 'there's that' 1.00, 'has that rare mix' 0.92, 'Legend has it' 0.34. 'gave it' 0.01, 'love that song' 0.02, 'has charm' 0.05. The pronoun is the trigger only after this verb.
